summary.name: Production Readiness Review (PRR) at Grafana Labs
summary.one_liner: A blog post describing how Grafana Labs built and runs a production readiness review process, in which experienced engineers review a product's checklist to find issues before on-call takes over.
use_cases: Setting up a production readiness review for a team without a dedicated SRE team
Designing a checklist for handing a service over to on-call
Running a multi-month reviewer-led review of a product before launch
Learning how Google's SRE practice of production readiness review was adapted in a smaller company
summary.what_it_does: The post explains Grafana Labs' production readiness review (PRR) process, which originated in Google's SRE book. Product teams fill in a PRR checklist, and a reviewer from outside the product team works through it in roughly 30-minute 1:1 sessions, often over 10 or more sessions spanning 2-3 months. Reviewers sometimes act as an attacker trying to break the system, and identified issues are filed as product bugs. The process ends once the issues are fixed. The author also describes checklist design advice, such as avoiding drift into architecture review, and planned follow-ups like periodic reviews.
notable: Reviews run as 30-minute 1:1 sessions with an experienced reviewer, usually from outside the product team
Checklist is meant to plug significant gaps with common sense rather than cover everything, and went through several versions after a canary round
Canary round surfaced a missing index file that could take down a service, along with tooling to fix it
caveats: Describes an internal process at Grafana Labs; the checklist snapshot is linked but its contents are not in the page text
Reviews can take 2-3 months, and the author notes answers may change quickly for pre-launch products
The process is still being developed; the post says the PRR had only just started
